stories.headline: France protests turn violent, with fires, looting and more than 1,200 arrests

sources.body:
Violence broke out across France on Saturday during the latest day of demonstrations against hardship in schools and the cost of living.

At least 1,200 people were arrested during what the French government described as an "escalation in violence" alongside an estimated 550,000 taking to the streets.

In Paris, there were significant clashes into the evening with riot police, who used tear gas and water cannon on crowds.

Buildings were set alight in the capital and other areas, including in Limoges where a large fire in the town hall caused the roof to partly collapse.

Looting broke out in several cities, with widespread vandalism targeting city halls and businesses also reported.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said 150 police officers were injured in the unrest.

In Paris, the main march appeared to be largely peaceful during the afternoon. A group of young people told the BBC they were "pacifists" who are "just trying to make things change, but nothing is moving".

However, as the day wore on some groups lit fires in the street and torched vehicles, including in iconic locations in the city centre like the Place de la République.

Shops were ransacked, at least one restaurant was gutted by fire, and the BBC saw fighting breaking out among some of the groups.

Riot police were seen charging at one crowd in central Paris and hitting several people with batons.

In Lyon, Mayor Grégory Doucet said the burning of the city's tourist office was "a tragedy" for the city, telling BFMTV "it breaks our hearts because it's a very iconic, well-known historic building".

Local police said "hostile individuals" prevented firefighters from safely tackling the blaze.

Fire crews also battled the fire at Limoges town hall, which the local prefecture said caused part of the building to collapse.

A young man "had his hand blown off by a grenade" in Saint-Étienne, the south-eastern city's Mayor Régis Juanico said on social media, adding: "Such a tragedy should never have happened."

The interior ministry said the protests involved "targeted acts of violence" from "hooded individuals" in places, including parts of the capital and also Marseille, Rennes, Toulouse and Angers.

Damage to buildings was reported across France, including in Grenoble, Avignon, Pau, Montpellier and Valence.

Clothes and food shops were raided in Paris, while an Apple store in Lille was broken into and emptied.

Footage authenticated by BBC Verify showed a tourist train in Grenoble being driven by masked men along a narrow street in the city centre towards at least three riot police officers.

Hundreds of thousands of students have protested in recent weeks over staff shortages and dilapidated facilities in the country's lycées - secondary schools attended by 15 to 18-year-olds.

On Saturday, their numbers were bolstered by trade union members and other protest groups.

These groups include the so-called gilets jaunes 'yellow vest' movement, who demonstrated against cost-of-living hikes for over a year from 2018 - becoming one of the longest-lived protest movements in French history.
sources.headline: Violent clashes, looting and buildings ablaze in France as over 1,000 arrested after protests

sources.body:
Police fire teargas in Paris and Limoges town hall ‘largely lost’ to fire – with officials blaming violence on ‘ultra-left’

More than 1,200 people were arrested in France on Saturday after protesters supporting high school students clashed with police, with some demonstrations later spiralling out of control as buildings were set ablaze and shops looted.

Police fired teargas in confrontations with protesters, as demonstrations across France were boosted by other groups angry about high prices and the fraying of a social welfare system. While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully in street marches in scores of cities, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, luxury boutiques and supermarkets and attacked police vehicles and officers.

Late on Saturday, prime minister Sébastien Lecornu said 1,200 people had been arrested and 150 police hurt.

Interior minister Laurent Nuñez said the official demonstration had been hijacked by casseurs – “ opportunistic delinquents who had seen a chance to pillage and loot … we will find them and deal with them firmly”.

He said the state was not planning to declare a state of emergency but added: “I very strongly condemn the violence we have seen.”

In the city of Limoges, the town hall was “largely lost” to a fire set by masked protesters, the top regional official told the AFP news agency.

“The roof has collapsed on to lower floors, except the west wing, and two-thirds of the exterior has already disappeared,” local prefect Maurice Barate, said, adding that the extensive damage to the 143-year-old building was a “catastrophe for heritage.”

In Marseille, protesters stormed the town hall, ramming the door with security barriers they removed from the street. They briefly managed to enter the municipal building, where a protester spray-painted an “A” for anarchy on a wall before the police removed them.

Around Place de la République in central Paris , a peaceful march turned violent, with police firing teargas at black-clad and masked rioters who threw fireworks and paving stones, attacked a bank and looted a sports shop. “We’re taking the Bastille!” one demonstrator yelled.

Others set wheelie bins on fire and threw firecrackers inside or pushed over glass recycling bins and picked up the bottles inside to use as missiles. A lorry was set on fire and flames spread to a nearby building.

Along Boulevard Magenta, one of the main south-north axis north of Place de la République running through a mostly working-class area, dozens of shops were broken into and looted.

Groups tried to break into the Galeries Lafayette department store, smashed banks, ransacked a Lacoste store and other boutiques and looted a mobile phone shop.

Residents in surrounding streets were forced to close windows and doors as huge clouds of teargas rose to roof level.

Saturday’s mobilisation followed calls on social media to revive the gilets jaunes (yellow vests) movement, which emerged in 2018 against social injustice.

The protests began last month at schools ⁠in the poor northern suburbs of Paris , where ⁠anger over teacher ​absences and shabby facilities quickly morphed into a nationwide movement against inequality, weak public spending and falling standards.
sources.headline: Buildings set ablaze and more than 1,200 arrested as police clash with protesters across France

sources.body: Protesters clashed with police in Paris and other French cities on Saturday as hundreds of thousands took to the streets to protest higher living costs and the declining conditions in schools and other public services. Several town halls were broken into – and in at least one instance set on fire – and many shops were vandalised and ransacked. One protester had his hand torn off by what appeared to be a crowd-control grenade used by police.
sources.headline: Fires and clashes rock France amid massive nationwide protests

stories.headline: Israeli settlers attack European diplomatic delegation in the West Bank

sources.body:
A delegation of European diplomats has been attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.

Belgium condemned the assault on its consul general and the other envoys and called for Israel to bring those responsible to justice.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) also condemned what they called "the severe act of violence" and said they were investigating.

But the office of the Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast doubt on what happened and suggested it was part of a "coordinated campaign to smear Israel".

The attack came only a day after a number of Palestinians and Heidi Levine, a Washington Post photographer, were injured in a separate assault by settlers in another village in the West Bank.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the attack on Levine was "disturbing" and "not a good look".

It was also condemned by the US Ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, who called it a "despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards". A staunch ally of Israel, Huckabee said the assailants must face "prosecution to the fullest extent of the law".

In Saturday's incident the European diplomats - from Belgium, France, Poland and the Catholic Church - had come to the largely Christian village of Taybeh near Ramallah.

They were there to assess the situation on the ground after almost near daily attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians trying to bring in their olive harvest.

Video footage from the scene showed masked settlers confronting the convoy. Reports suggest stones were thrown.

The Belgian authorities said a car from its consulate had a window smashed and a French mayor was assaulted. Video showed a man wearing a French tricolor sash slumped beside a vehicle.

Belgium's foreign minister Maxime Prevot condemned the attack and said Israel had a responsibility to bring those responsible to justice.

"Palestinians face this violence every day. Settlers also target journalists reporting on it and diplomats. Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack," he said.

"As the occupying power, Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice.

"Impunity for violent settlers must end. Belgium will continue to press for EU sanctions against those responsible for this violence and those who support them."

Gideon Sa'ar, Israel's foreign minister, said he strongly condemned the violence by what he called "Israeli rioters". He said the foreign ministry was in contact with the ambassadors of the countries involved.

But he added: "Without detracting from the severity of the incident, it is unfortunate that the visit was not coordinated with the IDF in advance. Such coordination could have helped safeguard the visitors' security."

The IDF said they "strongly condemn the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Israeli rioters."

"According to a preliminary inquiry, no IDF soldiers were present at the scene at the time of the attack," they added.
sources.headline: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank

sources.body:
French mayor and archbishop also attacked during violent attempt to stop Palestinians harvesting olives

Israeli settler militants have attacked European diplomats, a French mayor and the archbishop of Cambrai in Taybeh, in the occupied West Bank , injuring three people and damaging a car, in the latest violent attempt to prevent Palestinians from harvesting olives on their own land.

Bernard Baudoux, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, was wearing his red, white and blue sash of office and attempting to enter a vehicle with diplomatic plates when he was assaulted and knocked to the ground on Saturday.

The masked militant shouted “Vive la France” as he launched the attack, a witness said. Badoux’s wife, and Vincent Dollmann, archbishop of Cambrai, were also threatened by the group of seven men, some armed with clubs.

The group had joined the olive harvest on lands belonging to the Christian town of Taybeh, along with the French consul general in Jerusalem, his wife and other diplomats, and the Belgian and Polish consuls.

Settlers first attacked a group working on the lower slopes of hills near Taybeh. As well as stealing olives, they kicked, abused and assaulted a Palestinian woman in her 70s and beat a man so badly he needed six stitches for a head injury.

Then they approached the diplomats and Badoux, who was in Taybeh for the launch of a twinning agreement with his town in northern France. During the attack, the militants smashed the window of an armoured car belonging to the Belgian mission.

Maxime Prévot, Belgium’s deputy prime minister and minister of foreign affairs, condemned the violence against Palestinians, foreign diplomats and journalists, and said his country would continue to push for European Union sanctions on settlers.

“Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack,” he said. “This violence cannot be separated from Israel’s illegal settlement policy … the occupation of the Palestinian territory must end.”

Palestinian residents of Taybeh have lived with years of escalating attacks from Israeli militants, but settlers had never targeted foreign diplomats there, said Father Bashar Fawadleh, the town’s parish priest.

“What happened today is not an isolated incident. It represents a deeply disturbing escalation in settler violence,” Fawadleh said.

Since the start of the annual olive harvest in late September, Israeli militants have used violence to stop Palestinians bringing in a crop that is economically and culturally vital to their communities.

Since 27 September, settlers have launched more than 170 attacks, Israeli rights group Yesh Din said. They killed at least four people, injured more than 100 and damaged thousands of trees, according to Palestinian authorities.

Even the presence of Israeli activists, diplomats, senior clergy and journalists no longer serves as a deterrence to extreme violence.

“If such violence can take place before international witnesses, one must ask what protection remains for local families and farmers when those witnesses are no longer present,” Fawadleh said. “No individual should have to risk physical assault simply to harvest olives from their own land.”
sources.headline: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats in West Bank

stories.headline: Iran says two oil tankers caught fire after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz

sources.body:
The vessels, each carrying about two million barrels of crude oil, used an unauthorised route, the IRGC says.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has said two oil tankers, each carrying about two million barrels of crude oil, caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

The first tanker hit a mine, triggering an explosion and a “fierce fire”, the IRGC said on Saturday, while the second tanker hit a mine that engulfed it “in a massive blaze”, Iran’s official IRNA news agency reported.

Information about the ships’ names or the origin of their cargo was not immediately available.

IRNA said the vessels had switched off their positioning and radar systems and tried to use a route not authorised by Iran.

The IRGC also claimed that while one tanker tried to cross the waterway “with US support”, the second vessel was left immobilised.

Iran seized control of the Strait of Hormuz after the US-Israeli war on the country began in late February. Tehran has since demanded that all ships seek its authorisation before transiting. About one-fifth of global oil consumption transited the waterway before the war.

This week, IRGC naval commander Rear Admiral Ali Azmaei warned that any vessel that deactivated its navigation systems would be considered “hostile”.

The United States has imposed its own naval counter-blockade on Iranian oil exports.

Iran’s army earlier said that two tankers caught fire on Thursday and Friday in Tehran’s “prohibited zone” in the Gulf of Oman.

Maritime monitors also reported two tankers struck in Gulf waters off Saudi Arabia on Friday.

Last Sunday, six vessels were attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz, the most in a single day since the war began, according to security firm Vanguard, the International Maritime Organization and the UK maritime agency UKMTO.

Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past two weeks, with Iran saying it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions imposed last month.

Nearly 20.8 million barrels of oil passed through on October 8, but only 2.9 million on October 11, according to Kpler data.

The disruption has pushed up global energy prices and inflation.

US President Donald Trump has explicitly ruled out using a nuclear weapon against Iran. “I wouldn’t use nuclear,” he told the Newsmax news site in an interview on Thursday.

Trump said that he was also not considering putting troops on the ground in Iran. “No, I don’t see that, I don’t see it,” he said, adding he believes a deal to end the war will be reached after the November 3 US midterm elections.
sources.headline: Iran says two tankers catch fire after hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz

stories.headline: UAE agrees with Saudi Arabia to re-enter Yemen conflict amid Houthi gains

sources.body:
United Arab Emirates will reportedly resume payments to Yemeni forces as gains by Iran-backed Houthi fighters alarm Gulf state rulers

Yemen civil war: what sparked latest escalation and who is involved?

The United Arab Emirates has agreed to re-enter the Yemen conflict by resuming payments to some government forces fighting Iran-aligned Houthis in the south, according to sources in Yemen. In return, Saudi Arabia has agreed to provide air cover for the anti-Houthi force.

The new cooperation agreement is the first tangible sign that the deep rift between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over Yemen’s future is starting to be healed – if only because the advance by Houthi forces across Yemen has alarmed all the rival Gulf state rulers.

Saudi Arabia is facing daily drone and missile attacks and is struggling to maintain an atmosphere of normality, as Houthi strikes immobilise its airports and some of its energy infrastructure.

Southern forces – mainly in the Giant Brigades – were previously trained and funded by the UAE, and are regarded as some of the most effective in the disjointed anti-Houthi military coalition. But the UAE quit operations inside Yemen in January, cutting off its funding supply line.

Neither Saudi Arabia nor the UAE have responded to a demand this week by southern Yemen separatists for a referendum on secession, a move that would restore the 1967-1990 borders, when Yemen was two separate states.

The separatist Southern Transition Council has also not yet agreed for its troops to fight outside the borders of the old Southern Yemen, but an explicit agreement by Saudi Arabia to allow a referendum would be likely to lead to the lifting of that restriction.

Yemen’s UN-recognised government, based in Aden, declared last week a counteroffensive to drive Houthi forces from the capital Sana’a, but so far the military drive has met with limited success around Majzar near Marib and the Bab al-Mandab strait.

There is also no direct contact between the STC leader, Aidarous al-Zubaidi, and Saudi officials. Zubaidi fled to Abu Dhabi in January after a failed STC attempt to take charge across the south and announce a referendum on separation in two years’ time. In response, the Saudis bombed UAE arms shipments for STC forces.

The UAE then announced it was quitting all involvement in Yemen , and the Saudi-backed government said it would seek to try Zubaidi for treason.

UAE officials are deeply concerned by the state of the conflict. Despite massive losses, the Houthis are determined eventually to capture Taiz and Marib, the two remaining cities outside the boundaries of the old Southern Yemen.

On Friday two missiles fired by the Houthis struck the airport of Aden while a passenger plane was preparing to take off. No casualties were reported.

The missiles landed about 500 metres from the Yemenia Airways aircraft, and approximately 100 metres from the midpoint of the runway, said Yemen’s information minister, Moammar Al-Eryani.

The strike came a day after at least five people were killed and 16 injured in a Houthi attack on a presidential palace in Aden.
sources.headline: UAE agrees with Saudi Arabia to re-enter Yemen conflict amid Houthi gains

sources.body:
Forces intercepted and destroyed four drones over Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh, Eastern Province and southern region, coalition says.

The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis has said it intercepted and destroyed four drones over Riyadh and other regions, the latest in a wave of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s airports and oil facilities.

“We intercepted and destroyed four drones over the past few hours in the regions of Riyadh, the Eastern Province, and the South,” coalition spokesperson Major-General Turki al-Maliki said on Saturday.

He also posted footage of what he described as the air force intercepting cruise missiles and drones and striking ballistic missile launchers belonging to the Houthis.

Riyadh’s King Khalid airport has come under at least 20 attacks – including one last week that killed 13 people – since the fighting between the Houthi rebels and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government flared in July.

On Thursday, at least five people were killed in missile strikes near the presidential palace in Aden, the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognised government. It blamed the Houthis for the attack.

On Friday, the Yemeni government said the Houthis fired two missiles at Aden’s airport , while government forces said they had advanced in Marib province, northeast of Sanaa.

Saudi Arabia is backing a government counteroffensive, known as Dawn of Yemen, and has carried out air strikes on the Houthis, including on an oil facility in Sanaa.

Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi said on Saturday he was willing to “carry out any measure to protect” Saudi Arabia should the kingdom ask.

Egypt was not looking to intervene in regional wars, el-Sisi said, but it was “inconceivable” for Cairo to stand by while Saudi Arabia was harmed.

“I’m not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone. We are speaking only about defence,” he said.

Egypt’s parliament is holding an emergency session on Sunday at the president’s request.

Saudi Arabia has accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis’ escalation. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, meanwhile, said Tehran supported a “comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve” the conflict.

Several embassies in Saudi Arabia have restricted travel and warned citizens not to use airports.

The Saudi Ministry of Education extended remote learning for students in Riyadh and nearby Diriyah in light of the recent Houthi attacks.
sources.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts drones as Egypt weighs sending help

stories.headline: Deaths confirmed after major incident at Canadian military base

sources.body:
A large fire near a Canadian military base in Alberta has killed and injured some people, the defence minister said, without confirming the number of casualties.

The Canadian Armed Forces were working with local authorities to manage the fire and were looking into what caused it, David McGuinty said, describing the situation as "very, very active and delicate".

Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney said on X that a "serious incident creating a major fire" had occurred, adding his "thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected".

Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, where the fire broke out, is one of the country's busiest military training bases.

The blaze "spread rapidly due to high winds" and had torn through the fences of the base, the Municipal District of Wainwright said.

McGuinty told reporters he "cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory".

It is unclear when the fire broke out, but the district first posted about the incident at about 17:30 local time.

Local authorities have urged residents to avoid the area and give all emergency vehicles right of way.
sources.headline: Deaths confirmed in major fire at Canada military base

sources.body:
Incident at CFB Wainwright base in Alberta caused a ‘major fire’ that is spreading to the nearby town because of strong winds

People have been killed and injured after an incident at one of Canada’s busiest military training bases in Alberta caused a large fire, Canada’s defence minister said Saturday.

“I’m saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base,” defence minister David McGuinty said at a press conference on Saturday night.

McGuinty described the situation at CFB Wainwright as “active and delicate” with the fire being monitored very closely. “I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory”, he said at the press conference.

McGuinty did not provide casualty figures or details about what caused the incident. The Canadian Armed Forces and federal, provincial and local authorities were coordinating the emergency response, he said. The nearby community of Wainwright was providing hospital and firefighting support.

In an earlier social media post, prime minister Mark Carney said: “A serious incident creating a major fire has occurred at CFB Wainwright, in Alberta.”

“Our thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected,” he said.

The Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire crossed the base’s fence earlier Saturday and was spreading rapidly due to high winds. Firefighters from multiple jurisdictions were responding, and no evacuation order was in effect.

The Alberta premier, Danielle Smith, described the fire as “significant and tragic” and said it was affecting many military personnel.

Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, about 180km south-east of Edmonton, is one of Canada’s busiest military training bases, where soldiers prepare for combat operations. It is home to the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which conducts realistic battlefield exercises, and the 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre, which provides military training.

The Canadian conservative opposition leader, Pierre Poilievre, said he had spoken with Carney and the defence minister to offer support to those affected by the fire.

“Pray for Wainwright, everyone,” Poilievre said in a social media post. He urged people in the area to follow emergency instructions and keep roads clear for first responders.

Neither Carney nor Smith provided details about what caused the fire or whether anyone was injured.
sources.headline: ‘Serious incident’ at Alberta military base causes deaths and injuries, Canada officials say

stories.headline: Republican candidates keep Trump out of campaign advertising despite his rallies

sources.body: Donald Trump is barnstorming the country to boost Republicans in the final weeks of the midterms. But many candidates want to keep that support quiet. The president is nowhere to be found in GOP ads, even in red states where Republicans were happy to tout his endorsement two years ago. And some candidates are hesitant to appear with Trump on the campaign trail — even as they hope he will help juice turnout among the MAGA base in November. Democratic House and Senate candidates and outside groups have spent $145 million on general election ads mentioning Trump, while Republicans have spent just $8 million, according to a POLITICO analysis of data from AdImpact, which tracks political advertising. That’s in sharp contrast to 2024, when GOP candidates spent $62 million on ads mentioning Trump. “Trump is at historic lows right now, so if he comes to your district or state, it’s about getting the Republican base vote out there and that can certainly help,” said Ron Bonjean, a longtime GOP strategist. “But it's really important for the candidates not to be talking about Trump 24/7 on the campaign trail.” The unfavorable national political environment leaves few incentives for GOP candidates to tie themselves to Trump, and more and more Republicans in competitive races have broken with the president on issues such as the Iran war and tariffs. When Republicans do mention Trump in ads, they often aren’t touting his support. In Alaska, GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan has run an ad citing how he “voted to force Trump's DOJ to release the Epstein files.” The silence on the airwaves is especially stark in red states like Nebraska and Ohio. In 2024, Sen. Deb Fischer (R-Neb.), who was facing a challenge from independent Dan Osborn, and now-Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio), who was challenging then-Sen. Sherrod Brown, both ran several general election ads featuring endorsements from Trump. The president won Nebraska by more than 20 points and Ohio by 12 points that year, with Fischer and Moreno also winning their races. But this cycle, the GOP isn’t focusing its ads on Trump in either state, as the match-up between Osborn and Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts heats up in Nebraska and Brown seeks to oust Republican Sen. Jon Husted in Ohio. Both Ricketts and Husted appeared at Trump rallies earlier this month. Still, Trump is absent from all Republican Senate ads in Ohio, and the only Ricketts ads that name the president accuse Osborn of disparaging Trump supporters — but don’t mention Trump’s endorsement. "The war in Iran, I think, has become a real noose around the neck of Republican candidates because of the affordability crisis," said former Ohio Rep. Jim Renacci. A nonprofit he works with surveyed voters on whether GOP candidates should appear with Trump and found that "in most cases you do not want [Trump] standing near you, which is why I was a little bit surprised that Jon Husted has had two events with President Trump, because I do believe there's a strong headwind in Ohio, and a big change from 2024." Husted’s campaign spokesperson Amy Natoce told POLITICO in a statement, “President Trump won Ohio decisively three times by 8 points, 8 points and 11 points. If we successfully turn out the MAGA vote this November, then we will retire Sherrod Brown for good.” The National Republican Senatorial Committee did not respond to a request for comment. “President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party, and he is committed to maintaining Republican majorities in Congress,” White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said. “The choice has never been more clear: doubling down on President Trump’s winning, commonsense agenda or the Democrats’ extreme liberal policies and obstruction.” Another Republican operative, who is based in Ohio and like others was granted anonymity to speak candidly about their own party, said GOP candidates need to find a way to talk about the Trump administration — no tax on tips, protecting social security — without mentioning the guy in the Oval Office. “This is a historically unpopular president,” said the strategist, who has worked on multiple statewide races over the course of the last 15 years. “We all agree with that, and so it's kind of hard to attach yourself on the airways, I think, too closely to him.” Trump’s rallies, unlike candidates’ ads, are seen more as targeting the president’s base. He’s not only visiting traditional battlegrounds like Georgia and Michigan, but also typically safe red states like Alabama and Kansas. Still, his events have been a source of tension with some GOP candidates. When Trump’s team was making plans for the president to campaign in Michigan last week potentially in western Michigan, several Republican candidates and their teams up and down the ticket initially didn't know whether they should attend and be seen with the president, according to three Republicans with direct knowledge of the conversations, who were granted anonymity to share private details. They were concerned about being associated with Trump’s tariffs, which have hammered the state, along with high fuel prices amid the Iran war. Trump officials scrapped the event and said the president would visit the state later in the month. Trump is now scheduled for a rally in the state on Oct. 25. "[Republican candidates] are going to do what they need to do," said one GOP pollster close to the White House. "What the White House and the president are doing is they are targeting places where they think the president can be helpful.” Trump has allowed Republicans to discuss issues pertaining to their states or districts as “he understands that it is not a balk on him,” said one White House official, granted anonymity to speak candidly. If Trump “was to believe that all these individuals were balking him, I A) don’t think that he would want to be on the road every day, and B) I do think that you would probably see a more vocal President Donald J. Trump on Truth, et cetera, kind of voicing his opinion on it,” the official said. The president and his team are giving most Senate GOP candidates especially a wide latitude to break with some of his policies at times, according to two other White House officials involved in the conversations. Trump, they said, understands the need for vulnerable candidates to create some distance, even though in the past he has lashed out at members of his party for similar moves. Republicans in the more MAGA-friendly House, however, are expected to run more in lock-step with the president. Only the most at-risk candidates are afforded some room to break with Trump, the officials said, given the tidal wave of chaos that can spur within the conference. One GOP strategist working on a battleground House race, granted anonymity to discuss private information, said he had gotten pre-approved from the White House for his candidate to miss a planned rally. Still, the strategist cautioned, that doesn't mean Trump won't berate someone from the stage when he notices the candidate is missing. Republicans still see Trump as a unique motivator for his base and rallies as a tool to help turn out voters who might be driven by the president. With Democratic voters already energized by opposing Trump, the GOP has less to lose by bringing the president out to turn out MAGA voters too. “The reality is, Democrats are going to vote in this midterm,” said Paul Shumaker, a Republican strategist from North Carolina, where Trump is set to return for a rally next week as GOP Senate nominee Michael Whatley struggles to close the gap in his race. “And what Republicans need to be doing is focus on what they can do to improve their voter turnout on their side.” Lauren Fedor, Myah Ward, Andrew Howard and Alex Gangitano contributed to this report.
sources.headline: Not all Republicans want to show Trump off

stories.headline: Kansas Senate race becomes a serious liability for Republicans

sources.body: WICHITA, Kansas — Roger Marshall was running behind. The bus Kansas Republicans booked for a five-day barnstorming tour sat idling Tuesday morning, with other statewide candidates onboard. The tour was already a few minutes delayed as state party chair Danedri Herbert awaited word from the senator who some Republicans grumble isn’t campaigning hard enough as polls show him tied or trailing . Finally, she got word: Marshall would ride separately. As the bus reached its first stop in rural Newton, Marshall crept aboard — and was spotted by reporters doing so. He then joined the other candidates exiting to greet the crowd like he'd been there the whole time. Marshall is playing catch-up as he races to avoid becoming the first person to lose a Senate contest to a Democrat in the state in nearly a century. He faces the most serious challenger for a Kansas senator in over a decade as his party stares down a grim environment under President Donald Trump's second term. National Republicans are pouring millions into the state to prop him up; national Democrats are responding in kind, and Democrat Adam Hamilton, a well-known United Methodist pastor, is suddenly flush with cash for the campaign’s homestretch. But some Republicans think it’s already too late for Marshall. “He took it way too much for granted,” said former Kansas Gov. Mike Hayden, a Republican who supported Marshall’s previous campaigns but is now publicly backing Hamilton. “He's been almost invisible, except on national television. And there's not a lot of love in Kansas for Washington D.C.” National Republicans have privately urged Marshall to take his race more seriously on numerous occasions, according to a person familiar with the conversations who was granted anonymity to discuss them. Marshall, this person said, never appeared too worried about the race. Marshall’s latest Federal Election Commission report indicates this may be true. He raised just $866,000 for the third quarter to $9.9 million for Hamilton, and that filing did not appear to include any full-time payments to campaign staff. Marshall’s team did not respond to requests for comment on this article. One Republican strategist close to the White House, granted anonymity to speak candidly, acknowledged the race is an “uphill battle,” comparing Marshall to an “old athlete who, it takes them a lot longer to warm up to get ready for the game time, and they didn't start that early enough.” That strategist said that the remaining undecided voters are overwhelmingly Trump voters, and predicted they’d come home. Kansans “are mad at Republicans, but they just hate Democrats more,” the strategist said. “As much as DC Republicans are bedwetting, the ones actually working on the races are cognizant of this.” As the race nears the homestretch, a deluge of bad press has dogged the senator: His campaign used pictures of a Kansas campground without permission and had to edit the ad; his team faces accusations of blurring the line between his official and campaign offices; his campaign reportedly didn’t pay a bill to a local bakery for six years until after the unpaid debt was made public ( he apologized ). Two other stories landed the hardest. The first focuses on a Florida property that he owns, raising questions about how much time he actually spends in Kansas. The second stems from a New York Times report that Marshall, an obstetrician-gynecologist who served two terms in the U.S. House, had allegedly taken legal action against hundreds of medical patients who didn’t pay their bills. Marshall has said he spends the bulk of his time in Washington or Kansas, calling the claims “bologna.” He called the Times’ report a “hit job by left media” and told Fox News he had “nothing else to do to with the process” after patients’ accounts went to collections. At a Monday rally in the liberal college town of Lawrence, Hamilton told supporters that Kansans deserve a senator who isn’t just “showing up for photo ops” between “time with your family in Florida.” "I want to know from Roger Marshall: What's your plan when people … show up and they don't have health insurance?” Hamilton said, standing on a hay bale in a shady park. “Is the plan we're going to sue them? Then we're going to have some of them arrested, and maybe a few of them put in jail?" Hamilton’s campaign cut a face-to-camera ad with one of Marshall’s former patients, who said she was arrested when she was eight months pregnant because she missed a $50 payment to Marshall’s office. The Marshall campaign sent a cease-and-desist letter in response, saying the ad’s “message is false in every material respect,” and went up this week with its own ad of a former patient singing his praises. National Republicans have swooped in to prop up Marshall with $11 million in planned spending in recent days. And he’s getting other reinforcements: Chris Grant, the stalwart Trump-world operative and veteran of previous Marshall campaigns, will take an expanded role on the senator’s team through Election Day, Axios first reported . Marshall’s struggles are drawing unfavorable comparisons to the last Republican who needed to be bailed out to win a Senate race in the state. “This race reminds me of Sen. Pat Roberts’ last race [in 2014], when he was accused of not maintaining a Kansas residence and campaigning poorly,” said one Kansas state GOP lawmaker, who was granted anonymity to speak openly. But Republicans had a strong wind at their backs in 2014, sweeping nearly every Senate race that year; Roberts managed a 10-point win, similar to Marshall’s 11-point win in 2020. This time around, the national climate is blowing hard the other direction. Kansas has been especially hard-hit by some of Trump’s policies. His tariffs and spiking fuel prices left the state’s row crop farmers struggling. A plan to import cheap foreign beef infuriated ranchers in a state that produces the second-most cattle annually. And his threats to cut off U.S. sales of Bombardier planes — a Canadian company whose U.S. headquarters are in Wichita — rattled the state’s robust aviation industry. Marshall has recently shown signs he knows he’s in a fight. The normally strident MAGA backer broke with the president on the beef import plan and on a recent local immigration enforcement action, after ICE activity rattled some of his state’s agricultural towns. He’s banking on the conservative nature of the state, working hard to paint Hamilton as a progressive who will fall in line behind Washington Democrats. “This guy is the most radical liberal Democrat in the history of Kansas to get through a primary,” Marshall said in an interview in Garden City. “He is this wolf in sheep's clothing.” At rallies in Newton, Hutchinson, Dodge City and Garden City, he warned that his election could decide which party controls the upper chamber. “If my opponent were elected, it would give Chuck Schumer and AOC control of the Senate,” he repeated. Recent Republican ads hit Hamilton as “woke” and “radical,” pointing to his past praise of the Black Lives Matter movement. But as Marshall tagged along with the other GOP candidates for their barnstorming tour, holding mini-rallies across central and western Kansas on Tuesday, he was reminded how deep the anger at Washington runs right now — even in ruby-red Kansas. In Dodge City, the self-described “cattle capital” of the country, some Republicans in the crowd grumbled about spiking fuel prices. In Newton, protesters screamed through Marshall’s speech, calling Republicans “fascists.” (“Quiet, Satan!” a disgruntled attendee retorted.) In Garden City, where ICE activity sent shockwaves last month, Marshall got an earful in a private meeting with local lawmakers over their frustration that immigration officers barged into town without coordinating with local law enforcement. ”I think the frustration is still there,” state Rep. Jason Goetz, a Republican who represents some of the cities affected by ICE enforcement. There’s a belief among some Kansas Republicans that Marshall has thrown together so poor a campaign that if he wins, it won’t be of his own accord — it will be because of Ty Masterson, the Republican state Senate president running for governor who joined him on the bus tour and has polled a few points ahead of Marshall in most surveys. Rep. Tim Huelskamp, a Kansas Republican who lost a U.S. House primary to Marshall in 2016, said Masterson is “going to pull everybody across the line,” a list that “absolutely” includes Marshall. Patricia Woods, a Hutchinson resident, said at a rally that she is “100% behind Masterson.” When asked about Marshall, she said she is “kind of on the fence.” Masterson, when asked about Marshall’s race, simply chuckled. “It's more complicated than mine,” he said. Adam Wren and Andrew Howard contributed reporting.

sources.body:
Pedro Sánchez , ha insuflado ánimos a los socialistas con llamadas a la movilización este 29N para que haya una "ola progresista" en las urnas y ha metido de lleno a su mujer, Begoña Gómez , en la precampaña de las elecciones generales : "Querían quebrarnos y somos más fuertes". El presidente del Gobierno y secretario general del PSOE también ha lanzado un aviso a PP y Vox, y es que "las pensiones no se tocan" tras los comicios. Y la reacción entre los asistentes al acto en Fuenlabrada, después del Comité Federal, ha sido la euforia en un momento en que los socialistas confían en la "remontada".

Sánchez ha intervenido en Fuenlabrada (Madrid) después de un Comité Federal que ha ratificado las listas del partido a los comicios y tras haber sido designada Rebeca Torró nueva portavoz de los socialistas ante la dimisión de Montse Mínguez este viernes.

Sánchez, que ha animado a la movilización para cuatro años más de "avances" en lugar de "sacrificios y derogaciones", ha vuelto a asegurar que la causa de esta generación es la vivienda y ha prometido que el PSOE ganará esa batalla "como todas" las anteriores: "Con la fuerza de la gente y un gobierno progresista que llegue más lejos y antes gracias a una mayoría parlamentaria progresista".

Ha criticado que el PP y Vox solo tienen los "insultos", las "mentiras" y los "recortes de siempre". Pero ha lanzado un mensaje directo para Alberto Núñez Feijóo y Santiago Abascal: " Las pensiones no son un cheque regalado, son una conquista social lograda , así que un poco más de respeto a los mayores y más compromiso con nuestros mayores". "Las pensiones no se tocan. Si les gustan las motosierras, al aserradero ", ha espetado.

Se ha pronunciado así después de que la portavoz parlamentaria del PP, Ester Muñoz, asegurara esta semana que "el sistema de pensiones va a colapsar". Al respecto, ha recordado que cuando Mariano Rajoy abandonó el Gobierno había unos 5.000 millones de euros en la hucha de las pensiones y ahora hay "más de 20.000 millones".

Pero Sánchez ha revolucionado a los asistentes al inicio, cuando ha pedido ponerse una camiseta con el lema "la fuerza de la gente" y con una declaración de amor a su mujer, Begoña Gómez , imputada por el juez Juan Carlos Peinado por corrupción en los negocios. Con ella presente entre los asistentes, tras largo tiempo sin aparecer en un acto público junto a Sánchez, se ha dirigido a ella.

"Hoy me acompaña Begoña y quería darte las gracias. Sí, gracias por ser mi esposa, ser la madre de mis hijas y por ser mi mujer", ha aseverado. En ese momento, Gómez se ha levantado visiblemente emocionada a darle un beso y Sánchez, entre aplauso de los asistentes, ha proseguido: " Nos han intentado quebrar de todas las maneras y han logrado lo contrario . Estamos más unidos y somos más fuertes que nunca. Que lo escuchen alto y claro: te quiero ". "¡Qué bonito, qué bonito!", ha coreado el público.

Pero también ha revolucionado a los asistentes al final del acto, cuando se ha lanzado a bailar el tema 'Malibú' de Rusowsky, cuyo estribillo no ha pasado desapercibido tras el mensaje que ha lanzado a Begoña Gómez: "Ella es mi Tatiana, ella es mi Daisy, ella es mi mundo, ella es mi baby. Cuando estamos juntos to' desaparece . Todo en un segundo. ¿Dónde estás, mi baby?".

Alberto Núñez Feijóo (Orense, 1961) recibe a EL PERIÓDICO el miércoles en su despacho de la planta séptima de la sede del Partido Popular (PP) en la calle Génova. Segunda semana desde que Pedro Sánchez sorprendiera con el adelanto electoral para el 29-N, el presidente del PP dice estar dispuesto a batallar cada día para lograr unos resultados que le permitan acabar con lo que considera una "legislatura perdida" y poder "resetear el país" tras los años de mandato de Pedro Sánchez.

PREGUNTA: Esta semana, los Reyes han ido a Ceuta y Melilla, ¿cómo valora la visita y qué horizonte de solución hay en la mesa a la crisis en la ciudad autónoma?

RESPUESTA: La Jefatura del Estado, los Reyes de España han estado a la altura de nuestro país. Al final, son los que han dicho dos cosas fundamentales. Primero, la integridad de la soberanía española no se negocia. Segundo, todos los que han entrado irregularmente se tienen que ir de forma inmediata. Esos dos principios si los hubiese asumido el Gobierno de España desde hace más de dos meses, no tendríamos la crisis que hemos tenido. Y adicionalmente nos vamos enterando de más cosas.

Nos vamos enterando de que buques de la Marina marroquí estaban en aguas españolas cuando se producía la invasión. Nos estamos enterando a través, espero, del sumario de la Audiencia Nacional, de cómo el Gobierno mintió de forma reiterada. Cómo el Gobierno lo sabía y no actuó. Cuando Sánchez dice que aquellos días fueron días duros, hombre, no me diga usted que el presidente del Gobierno dice que hay días duros y lo que hace es irse de vacaciones durante 25 días a una residencia oficial viendo cómo se violenta la integridad territorial de tu país, cómo una ciudad española de 80.000 habitantes es invadida por 80.000 o 100.000 extranjeros, cómo hay buques en aguas jurisdiccionales españolas y cómo no hace nada.

Entrevista a Alberto Núñez Feijóo / José Luis Roca

Menos mal que tenemos al jefe del Estado, al rey de España, que ha dicho muy claramente : aquello es español desde hace 500 años y por lo tanto España no se negocia. No le pedimos nada a ninguna otra potencia, salvo respeto. Y si no nos respetan, tienen que ver firmeza. Esto es lo que ha venido a decir el rey de España. Yo, desde luego, estaría con el rey de España acompañándole en esta visita trascendental e histórica que los Reyes han hecho esta semana a Ceuta.

P: Tres únicas visitas de tres reyes en cien años.

R: Y creo que hay un antes y un después de la invasión de Ceuta. El 2 de septiembre, cuando se llenaron todas las plazas de España, las calles de España, yo mismo me quedé sorprendido. Yo estuve esa mañana en Ceuta, llegué para la manifestación. Cuando vi cómo estaba Madrid, cuando posteriormente me pasaron los vídeos de Pamplona, de Bilbao, de Santiago, de Barcelona… comprendí que la gente había tomado muy buena nota sobre la integridad territorial de nuestro país. Me dijeron, no lo sé, que había salido más gente a la calle que el día del asesinato de Miguel Ángel Blanco. No lo sé. Lo que sí sé es que es un antes y un después.

Després de les hores de tensió viscudes abans de la fi del termini per presentar coalicions i el fracàs en les converses per arribar a un acord amb Podem, aquest dissabte el Front Ampli ha presentat el seu projecte polític a Madrid.

Ada Colau , candidata a la presidència per la llista de Barcelona, defensa que han buscat l'acord "fins a l'últim minut" i amb "extrema generositat". Reconeix que han decebut, i tot i que assegura que han tingut la mà estesa a Podem, diu que "no es pot obligar algú que no vol seure a taula" .

Colau ha fet una crida a la mobilització de l'esquerra per capgirar les enquestes. Diu que és l'hora de donar protagonisme a la gent, en un moment històric en què cal "derrotar a les urnes el feixisme" . Per aquesta raó, afegeix, cal no equivocar-se d'adversari, generar esperança i respondre als anhels d'unitat dels votants.

El dret a l'habitatge és la carta de presentació del Front Ampli. Per Colau, la seva candidatura és l'única garantia davant d'un PSOE i un Pedro Sánchez massa curt.

A la mateixa hora, Podem contraprogramava un acte a Madrid en què Irene Montero ha acusat el Front Ampli de boicotejar a última hora el pacte en territoris on ja s'havien tancat acords: "Teníem acords avançats en molts territoris."

Montero ha demanat "perdó per l'espectacle" en la negociació infructuosa entre els partits de l'esquerra, però posa en valor el pacte assolit amb ERC per concórrer a les eleccions del 29N a Catalunya amb Gabriel Rufián.

Montero ha reconegut que era difícil arribar a un acord amb el Front Ampli "no per les llistes, ni pels llocs", sinó perquè fa anys que mantenen "discrepàncies polítiques serioses" amb formacions com Sumar. "Som molt crítics amb la seva forma de governar i amb la seva proximitat amb el PSOE."

En un acte a Fuenlabrada, que s'ha convertit en un míting, el Comitè Federal del PSOE ha aprovat les llistes de cara al 29N i ha proclamat per unanimitat Pedro Sánchez com a candidat. L'acte ha tingut com a protagonista sorpresa Begoña Gómez, la dona del president del govern espanyol.

Sánchez ha fet entrar Begoña Gómez en campanya amb tota una declaració d'amor just quan ella està a punt de seure al banc dels acusats per presumptes delictes de tràfic d'influències i malversació.

"Han intentat trencar-nos de totes les maneres possibles. Ara som més forts que mai. Que ho sentin alt i clar: t'estimo", ha proclamat Sánchez mirant la seva parella i convidant-la a pujar a l'escenari.

Sánchez ha fet una crida a la mobilització per aturar "l'onada reaccionària", evitar que Espanya "retrocedeixi quatre dècades" i s'ha mostrat confiat que el 29N els socialistes continuaran a La Moncloa. Ha carregat durament contra PP i Vox i ha dit que el salari mínim interprofessional i les pensions tornaran a pujar aquest any.

Des de la Garriga, Miriam Nogueras ha reivindicat la capacitat de Junts per aturar "els dos blocs espanyols" , que considera que cada cop estan més condicionats pels extrems. Al Consell Nacional de Junts, la candidata ha defensat que les eleccions del 29N decidiran "la capacitat de Catalunya de defensar-se i de fer que Madrid treballi per a Catalunya i no a l'inrevés".

stories.headline: Storm Adam brings torrential rain warnings across Spain's Mediterranean coast

sources.body:
Los efectos de la dana Adam ya se notan en gran parte de España. La madrugada del domingo traerá chubascos y tormentas fuertes o muy fuertes en Cataluña y el sureste peninsular; durante el resto del día, fuertes o muy fuertes en Andalucía, Murcia, Ceuta y Melilla, y muy fuertes o torrenciales y con acumulados importantes, incluso de más de 300 litros por metro cuadrado en 24 horas, en las islas Pitiusas, Valencia y el norte de Alicante . Rachas de viento muy fuertes en el litoral valenciano. Descenso notable (más de 6 grados) de las temperaturas máximas en la mitad este peninsular y de las mínimas en las montañas del centro peninsular.

Se espera un día inestable en la Península y Baleares por la influencia de una masa de aire frío en altura y la formación de dos danas: Adam al norte, sobre Francia, y otra al sudoeste de la Península. Así, predominarán los cielos poco nubosos en el noroeste y muy nubosos o cubiertos en el resto. Se darán precipitaciones en la mayor parte del territorio, con algunas lloviznas o lluvias débiles y dispersas en el Cantábrico y la meseta norte y chubascos y tormentas fuertes o muy fuertes en el tercio sur peninsular, Ceuta y Melilla.

En Cataluña y el sureste peninsular de madrugada, es probable que los chubascos y tormentas sean muy fuertes, y durante el día en las islas Pitiusas, Valencia y el norte de Alicante, torrenciales y con acumulados importantes, incluso de más de 300 litros por metro cuadrado en 24 horas. En Canarias, se esperan cielos nubosos y precipitaciones en el norte de las islas montañosas e intervalos nubosos en el resto con alguna precipitación ocasional.

Son probables las brumas y nieblas matinales en el entorno mediterráneo y en zonas de montaña del norte y sureste.

Se prevé un descenso generalizado de las temperaturas, de forma ligera en los archipiélagos. Por el contrario, los descensos serán más notables en la mitad este peninsular para las máximas y en las montañas del centro para las mínimas. Se darán heladas débiles en montañas del norte. Las mínimas se alcanzarán al final del día en amplias zonas de la Península.

Soplará viento del norte y nordeste en la mayor parte del país, con cierzo en el Ebro. Se prevé moderado en la mitad norte peninsular y los archipiélagos y con intervalos fuertes y probables rachas muy fuertes en el litoral valenciano. Únicamente en el sur e interior sureste peninsular soplará del este, moderado en el Estrecho y Alborán y flojo en el resto.

Aemet ha emitido un aviso rojo por lluvias, tormentas, viento y fenómenos costeros en la Comunidad de Valencia. El nivel de aviso es naranja en Andalucía, Baleares y Murcia, manteniéndose el amarillo en Cataluña, Extremadura, Galicia, Ceuta y Melilla

sources.body:
Ambiente de lluvia en Barcelona, 5 de octubre de 2026 / Pau Gracià / EPC

La Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet) ha emitido un nuevo aviso sobre la llegada de la dana que, según confirman los modelos, llegará a España este fin de semana. La entidad advierte que el fenómeno arrancará el sábado con el descuelgue y aislamiento de una dana sobre el norte de la Península Ibérica y que, a raíz de ello, desde ese día se producirá un aumento generalizado de la inestabilidad que desembocará en un "nuevo episodio de precipitaciones intensas y persistentes" en el Mediterráneo que elevará de nuevo el riesgo de inundaciones locales. Los pronósticos apuntan ahora al domingo y al lunes como los días más potencialmente adversos de este episodio, con chubascos torrenciales que podrían afectar a amplias zonas de Catalunya, Murcia, Málaga y Baleares. Los expertos afirman que dada la incertidumbre asociada a este fenómeno habrá que mantenerse atentos a futuras actualizaciones de los modelos para entender cuáles serán los puntos más afectados por este nuevo episodio de lluvias torrenciales.

Los modelos apuntan a que la primera dana de este otoño podría dejar intensas lluvias torrenciales en prácticamente toda la costa mediterránea y sumar acumulaciones de entre 150 y 250 litros por metro cuadrado en periodos muy cortos de tiempo. Los expertos afirman que es probable que el episodio venga acompañado de intervalos de viento fuerte y temporal marítimo. Dada la intensidad del episodio, las autoridades afirman que las intensas lluvias derivadas de esta dana podrían producir "inundaciones locales, especialmente en zonas bajas, así como crecidas repentinas en arroyos y ramblas, sobre todo en áreas con suelos saturados por anteriores episodios de precipitación" por lo que se pide a la población extremar las precauciones.

Los especialistas afirman que aún no está del todo claro cuál será la trayectoria y la intensidad de esta dana ya que, hasta ahora, los modelos se muestran aún inciertos sobre la evolución de este fenómeno. Pero según explica la Aemet, en estos momentos todo apunta a que de cara al domingo lo s mayores acumulados podrían darse en áreas del este de Catalunya , norte del cabo de La Nao, litorales de Alicante y Murcia, área de la Costa del Sol e islas Pitiusas . El lunes, en cambio los máximos de precipitación podrían continuar afectando al entorno del cabo de La Nao y costa del Sol, y extenderse a zonas del sur de Catalunya y de su extremo oriental, así como al resto de las islas Baleares.
sources.headline: La Aemet señala el domingo y el lunes como los días más adversos de la dana y advierte de lluvias torrenciales en toda la costa mediterránea

stories.headline: Storm disrupts Barcelona airport, while emergency services search for missing woman near Cabrera de Mar

sources.body: El Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya ha elevat els avisos per pluja a Barcelona , un episodi que arriba quan encara són presents els efectes del darrer temporal, de principis d’octubre. En previsió de forts aiguats, aquest dissabte, hi ha set comarques en avís vermell , entre les quals hi ha el Barcelonès, i 10 més en avís taronja. De moment, els aiguats han descarregat amb força al Vallès Oriental i al Maresme , on els Bombers busquen una dona desapareguda després de caure a la riera de Cabrera de Mar. A Barcelona, els xàfecs van per barris. Tot i això una potent tempesta ha aturat temporalment l’operativa a l’aeroport del Prat i ha provocat múltiples retards i cancel·lacions. Davant la previsió meteorològica adversa, Protecció Civil té activada l’ alerta del pla Inuncat i ha enviat un missatge ES-Alert a les comarques que estan en avís vermell amb recomanacions per reduir la mobilitat. En aquesta pàgina pots seguir minut a minut l’ última hora d’aquesta alerta per pluges intenses a Barcelona i Catalunya i totes les afectacions.  També et pot interessar Avís vermell per pluja intensa a Barcelona: Protecció Civil envia un ES-Alert amb recomanacions Marta Casals Torres Sílvia Gutiérrez 3 minuts de lectura

sources.body:
La dana Adam ha irrumpido este sábado con fuerza en el litoral mediterráneo, especialmente, en Cataluña, donde los servicios de emergencia buscan una persona desaparecida tras caer a la riera en Cabrera de Mar, Barcelona , que bajaba muy crecida como consecuencia de las lluvias torrenciales que afectan a la comarca del Maresme.

En una entrevista al Canal 24 Horas, el alcalde de la localidad, Óscar Fernández, ha asegurado que las autoridades —seis dotaciones de los Bomberos y efectivos de los Mossos d'Esquadra y de Salvamento Marítimo— están "trabajando intensamente" para encontrarla, después de que recibieran el aviso sobre las 19:40 horas . "La jornada está siendo dura. Hasta donde recuerdo no había pasado nunca en la región. Es una noche trágica y esperemos que tenga un buen desenlace", ha indicado para después cifrar en "60 litros en 40 minutos" las precipitaciones caídas en la localidad.

En Sentmenat, la comarca del Vallès Occidental, los bomberos también han rescatado a dos personas que estaban atrapadas por el agua dentro de un coche . La lluvia también ha afectado de nuevo a Granollers, una de las ciudades más dañadas por las excepcionales precipitaciones de hace quince días en Cataluña, que dejaron tres fallecidos.

Los ciudadanos de la comarca gerundense de La Selva y las barcelonesas de Maresme, Vallès Oriental y Vallès Occidental, Barcelonès, Baix Llobregat, Garraf , así como los de la ciudad de Granollers (Barcelona) han recibido este sábado un mensaje Es-Alert en sus móviles en el que se les alertaba de lluvia puntualmente torrencial a lo largo de la jornada y hasta las dos de la madrugada.

Desde las 22:00 horas, la circulación de trenes de cercanías de la R2 Sur está interrumpida y los trenes regionales hacia el sur se desvían por Vilafranca, Barcelona. La suspensión permanecerá vigente hasta que mejoren las condiciones meteorológicas y se compruebe que el estado de la infraestructura permite reanudar el servicio con garantías de seguridad.

Las lluvias también ha tenido especial incidencia en Albacete y Almería, con centenares de afecciones. En dicha provincia andaluza, uno de los territorios más afectados ha sido El Ejido, que tenía un aviso rojo y en el que han caído más de 100 litros por metro cuadrado (l/m2) en una hora, que han motivado la suspensión de todas las actividades de carácter municipal.

Tanto allí como en toda la comarca de Poniente, el 112 Andalucía ha recibido más de un centenar de incidencias : vehículos atascados, grandes acumulaciones de agua, desbordamiento de ramblas e inundaciones de locales, bajos y sótanos. Además, las autoridades andaluzas han elevado el Plan de Emergencias ante el Riesgo de Inundaciones a fase de emergencia, situación operativa 1 y han lanzado un Es-Alert para evitar desplazamientos , no cruzar zonas anegadas ni cauces y estar cerca de zonas elevadas.

La inestabilidad ha estado, asimismo, a lo largo y ancho de la Península con fuertes episodios de viento, temporal marítimo y tormentas, a excepción de puntos en el interior. La entrada del frente frío también ha hecho descender las temperaturas en la mitad norte y a nivel general.

Granollers o cómo tropezar dos veces con la misma piedra tras la tormenta del 5 de octubre 

Se cumplieron los pronósticos. El frente anunciado el viernes por la tarde y ayer por la mañana por el Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya barrió el prelitoral y el litoral tal y como estaba previsto, quizás con algo más de virulencia de lo esperado. Las redes sociales no suelen ser una fuente fiable, pero permitieron, con el testi­monio visual ciudadano, seguir el avance del temporal, de nuevo con tintes tropicales, acompañado de un potente viento, con precipitaciones que en algunos casos llegaron a acumular 64 litros por metro cuadrado, como fue el caso de Cabrils. Hoy no pinta tan mal, pero para el lunes se otea un nuevo aguacero.

Precisamente en el Maresme, en Cabrera de Mar, una mujer cayó a la riera y al cierra de esta edición los bomberos seguían buscándola. Se trata de una vecina de Malgrat de Mar, madre de familia de unos 40 años, muy conocida. La familia se habría visto sorprendida por la crecida del cauce y la mujer había caído junto a una de sus hijas. El padre se ha lanzado al agua y ha conseguido salvar a la niña, informa Fede Cedó.

Santa Maria de Palautordera, Mataró, Premià de Mar, Vilassar de Mar, Llinars, Granollers. Y más tarde, Barcelona y su entorno metropolitano. El temporal cepilló Catalunya de este a oeste, con especial crudeza en las comarcas de La Selva, Maresme y Vallès Oriental, que a las 13.20 horas fueron las primeras en recibir un ES-Alert. La mañana fue tranquila. Hasta mediodía, cuando empezaron a formarse nubes y en el radar del Meteocat pudo verse ese color rojo que no augura nada bueno.

En esas zonas con alerta máxima se anunciaban lluvias torrenciales y se recomendaba minimizar la movilidad y no acercarse a zonas inundables. Eso implica retirar los coches de las rieras, pero una vez más se vieron automóviles cortando el paso del agua. A las 16.20 horas Protecció Civil también irrumpió en los teléfonos del Vallès Occidental, Barcelonès, Baix Llobregat y Garraf, con un mensaje que en catalán alargaba la alarma hasta las dos de la madrugada y en castellano la reducía a la medianoche. Un fallo tonto. Poco después de las 20 horas se enviaba una notificación a Granollers, epicentro del terrible temporal del 5 de octubre. La localidad superó en algunos pluviómetros los 50 l/m2.

Mientras la borrasca avanzaba, seis dotaciones de bomberos, junto a Mossos d’Esquadra y salvamento marítimo, buscaban a la mujer que había caído a la riera, alimentada por el agua que se desliza desde la montaña de Burriac y su entorno. No muy lejos de ahí, en la carretera N-II, los automóviles avanzaban con el agua a medio neumático. Sin incidentes, más allá de dos personas mayores rescatada de su vehículo en Sentmenat.

Andrés Actis Fernández, Natalia Palazón, Mario Chaparro

Cabrils, a nada de Cabrera, marcó ayer el récord histórico de precipitación acumulada en solo 10 minutos de la red de estaciones automáticas gestionadas por el Servei Meteorológic de Catalunya: fueron 37,8 litros por metro cuadrado; según los que saben, una barbaridad.

sources.body: TMB ha instal·lat barreres antiinundacions en un dels accessos de l’estació de Parc Logístic, de l’L9S, davant la previsió de pluges torrencials per a aquest vespre a Barcelona . Aquestes tanques són unes estructures de plàstic en forma de ela que permeten desviar l’aigua i evitar així inundacions a les instal·lacions i equipaments de l’estació. Es tracta d’una prova pilot i s’ha escollit la parada de Parc Logístic perquè va ser una de les més afectades per les inundacions causades per les tempestes de principis d’octubre . Joan Granés, responsable de manteniment d’infraestructures, estacions i túnels de metro de Barcelona, explica que TMB ha iniciat els tràmits per comprar barreres d’aquest tipus , que s’utilitzarien a diferents estacions en casos d’episodis de pluges torrencials. “Estem mirant diferents proveïdors que ens el puguin subministrar, avui fem la prova pilot i en funció de l’èxit que tingui aquesta prova farem una compra més endavant de més material”. També et pot interessar Avís vermell per pluja intensa a Barcelona: Protecció Civil envia un ES-Alert amb recomanacions Marta Casals Torres Sílvia Gutiérrez 3 minuts de lectura Fàcils de posar i treure Les barreres que s’han instal·lat al metro han estat cedides pels Bombers de Barcelona , que són també els qui les han col·locat en aquesta primera prova al metro. Són les mateixes tanques que es van col·locar amb èxit a l’escola i l’institut Bosc de Montjuïc i que van evitar inundacions posteriors a tot dos centres. Aquestes estructures són d’instal·lació fàcil i ràpida i permeten d’una manera efectiva desviar l’aigua per protegir els diferents equipaments. “Són molt fàcils de posar, i molt fàcils de treure i aquesta és la virtut”, explica el cap d’unitat de Bombers de Barcelona, Carlos Chico Tapias, ” actuen de manera molt ràpida, quan més forta està l’aigua, més fort s’arrela al paviment”. També et pot interessar Tanques provisionals a l’escola i l’institut Bosc de Montjuïc, un nou aliat contra les inundacions Marta de San Nicolás 2 minuts de lectura Ús de sacs de sorra De moment, TMB ha iniciat els tràmits per comprar barreres d’aquest tipus per utilitzar-les a diferents estacions en casos d’episodis de pluges torrencials. Mentre no es disposi d’aquestes estructures, TMB ha previst altres maneres de protegir els accessos a les estacions, com ara l’ús de sacs de sorra per contenir l’entrada d’aigua.

TMB ha instalado barreras antiinundaciones en uno de los accesos a la estación de Parc Logístic de la línea 9 ante la previsión de lluvia para la tarde-noche de este sábado.

Es la primera vez que se instalan estas estructuras. Son de plástico, tienen forma de L y evitan que el agua se filtre en las instalaciones.

Durante el episodio de lluvias torrenciales de principios de octubre, esta estación se vio afectada por la entrada de agua. Los Bombers de Barcelona han cedido las barreras.

TMB ha iniciado los trámites para adquirir este tipo de estructuras y utilizarlas en diferentes estaciones durante episodios de lluvias torrenciales. Mientras no disponga de ellas, se seguirán empleando otros métodos, como los sacos de arena , para proteger las instalaciones.

sources.body: (ACN) L’alcalde de Badalona, Xavier García Albiol , serà el candidat del PP per Barcelona a les eleccions generals del 29-N . Així ho han confirmat aquest dissabte els populars en una publicació a X, després que algunes veus apuntessin des de fa setmanes que Albiol seria el cap de files per la circumscripció electoral. “ Un fitxatge de gran alçada per a una Espanya que necessita persones amb idees clares”, han escrit. El líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, té previst visitar aquest diumenge Barcelona per oferir un acte de precampanya al Palau de Congressos de Catalunya. També et pot interessar Carlos Prieto plega com a delegat del Govern a Catalunya per anar amb el PSC a les generals del 29-N Marina Segura i Vidal Roger Torres i Liñán 1 minut de lectura “Seguiré sent alcalde” Ara bé, Albiol ha assegurat que continuarà sent alcalde de Badalona : “El meu compromís de present i futur amb la meva ciutat segueix intacte”, ha defensat. En aquest sentit, ha acceptat ser candidat per “ acabar amb les ocupacions il·legals , combatre la multireincidència i controlar la immigració irregular ” des del Congrés. sources.body:
Xavier García Albiol serà el candidat del Partit Popular per Barcelona a les eleccions del 29N. El partit ha confirmat, en un missatge a X, que l'alcalde de Badalona encapçalarà la llista dels populars a la demarcació barcelonina.

El PP presenta García Albiol com "un fitxatge d'alçada" en un missatge dirigit a Fabrizio Romano –un periodista esportiu italià especialista a revelar abans que ningú fitxatges de futbol– a qui diuen, irònicament "aquesta no l'has vist venir".

A més, sota la foto d'Albiol, els populars hi han afegit la frase "Here we go", una expressió que utilitza habitualment aquest periodista a les xarxes socials abans d'anunciar una primícia.

Just després d'aquest anunci, García Albiol ha fet també una piulada a X en què ha confirmat que el president del Partit, Núñez Feijóo, li ha demanat que lideri la llista per Barcelona i que "accepta la responsabilitat amb orgull, il·lusió i un enorme sentit de compromís".

Albiol afegeix, al missatge, que continuarà sent alcalde de Badalona i que posa entre les prioritats del seu mandat com a diputat "acabar amb les ocupacions il·legals, combatre la multireincidència i el control de la immigració il·legal".

Os quiero informar de que @NunezFeijoo me ha pedido que sea el candidato del @ppopular por la provincia de Barcelona en las Elecciones Generales del próximo 29 de noviembre. Acepto esta responsabilidad con orgullo, ilusión y un enorme sentido del compromiso. Quiero dejar algo muy claro: voy a seguir siendo alcalde de #Badalona y mi compromiso de presente y futuro con mi ciudad sigue intacto. Ahora quiero llevar la voz de Badalona y del resto de municipios de Cataluña al Congreso de los Diputados, para defender temas que afectan directamente a nuestros vecinos: acabar con las ocupaciones ilegales, combatir la multirreincidencia y el control de la inmigración irregular.

La resta de caps de llista del PP a Catalunya per demarcacions són: Roger Melero per Lleida, Diana Moya per Girona i Mónica Landete perTarragona.

L'anunci s'ha fet un dia abans de la visita prevista a Barcelona del líder del Partit Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo , que aquest diumenge farà un acte de precampanya al Palau de Congressos de Catalunya.

Els quatre caps de llista de les demarcacions de Catalunya estaran presents a l'acte preelectoral del PP a Barcelona d'aquest diumenge.
